questions.stem: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:

options.option_text: President on the recommendation of the outgoing Chief Justice (convention: seniormost judge)

questions.explanation: By convention (not law), the outgoing CJI recommends the seniormost judge of the SC. The President formally appoints. The collegium (CJI + 4 senior judges) recommends all SC appointments.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Supreme Court of India was established in:
questions.explanation: Supreme Court of India established 28 January 1950 (2 days after Republic Day). Replaced the Federal Court of India (1937-1950). First CJI: H.J. Kania.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Article gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction (power to hear cases directly)?

options.option_text: Article 131 — disputes between states, or between states and the Centre

questions.explanation: Article 131: SC has exclusive original jurisdiction in disputes between (a) two or more states, (b) Union and states. This cannot be bypassed by going to the High Court first.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A High Court judge holds office until the age of:

options.option_text: Till retirement as set by Parliament

questions.explanation: High Court judges: retirement age 62. Supreme Court judges: retirement age 65. Removed only by Parliament by address (like President) — same procedure as SC judges.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was evolved in India by:

options.option_text: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer in the late 1970s

questions.explanation: PIL (1970s-80s): Indian innovation — Justice Bhagwati and Krishna Iyer allowed relaxed locus standi (any citizen could approach SC for public interest). India's PIL system is unique globally.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The concept of 'judicial review' in India is derived from which country?
questions.explanation: Judicial review: borrowed from the USA (Marbury v. Madison, 1803 established the principle). India's version is more limited — courts can strike down laws violating the Constitution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: How many permanent judges (including CJI) can the Supreme Court have?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019: increased strength to 34 (CJI + 33 judges). Original Constitution: CJI + 7 (1950). Gradually increased to meet workload.
questions.subject: Polity
